parts.part: the ETT notion of an extension and its corollary
parts.note: IsSpacetimeExtension CN C ι: IsOpenEmbedding ι, range ι ≠ univ, ChartIso CN C (toOpenPartialHomeomorph ι) (chartSource = ⊤, chartImage U = ι '' U). The hypotheses on N (causally arc-connected, future one-connected: nodes) pass to W = ι(N); exists_leaving_futureInextensible_of_isOpenEmbedding locates the extension; δ = ι⁻¹ ∘ γ is chronal in N on every [0, s] (ChartIso.chronalCurveOn_symm_image) and future-inextensible in N (futureInextensible_of_forall_not_tendsto: a limit n of δ at 1⁻ would make γ 1 = ι n, T2).

The timelike line with W = (−∞, 0) satisfies every hypothesis of the assembly; exp : ℝ → ℝ is an extension of the timelike line into itself onto (0, ∞) (a strictly increasing open embedding is a ChartIso, by intermediate_value_Icc) and satisfies every hypothesis of the corollary. ExitDiamonds puts the curve segment in the identified diamond, so the identification is between non-empty sets.

findings: Thm 4.9's proof (:798) writes 'Without loss of generality we can assume that γ is future directed (otherwise reverse the time orientation of M_max)', and the next sentence (:800) uses 'Since ∂_u and ∂_v are future directed'. After a reversal of the time orientation, fixed by ∂_u + ∂_v future directed (:706, :752), ∂_u and ∂_v are past directed. The reduction needs a time-orientation-reversing isometry of M_max, for instance (u, v, ω) ↦ (−u, −v, ω). It preserves H (uv < const, :671, :748) and g_max, which depends on uv and on du⊗dv + dv⊗du (:704, :750), and it sends ∂_u + ∂_v to its negative. This step is not stated; it is harmless. In ETT the reversal is C.dual, and every hypothesis of the skeleton is two-sided (dual_causallyArcConnectedOn, dual_futureOneConnectedOn, dual_locallyStronglyCausal, dual_hasChronalNeighbour), so layer 1 has no gap.

Outside this target's rows (§4.1, the Kruskal model; T-loc-schwarzschild-model): :721 (d = 3) states that (u, v, ω) ↦ (t_A, r, ω) is a time-orientation-preserving isometry onto M_ext for A ∈ {I, IV} and onto M_int for A ∈ {II, III}. Along a future-directed curve u and v increase (∂_u + ∂_v future, :706). On IV = {u > 0, v < 0} (:676), t_IV = 2m log(−v/u) (:718) then decreases, while ∂_t is future directed on M_ext (:654). On III = {u < 0, v < 0} (:675), uv decreases, so r = F̃⁻¹(−uv) (:698) increases, while −∂_r is future directed on M_int (:664). So the maps are time-orientation reversing for A = IV and A = III, and preserving for I and II only. It is harmless where it is used (:809, 'since both regions are isometric'): the swap (u, v) ↦ (v, u) maps IV onto I, preserving uv, du⊗dv + dv⊗du and ∂_u + ∂_v. The d > 3 sentence (:752) makes no orientation claim.

§1 (:153–158) states the identification (1.2) with I^±(·, M_max). It justifies it by 'the exterior of the Schwarzschild black hole is future one-connected, i.e., in particular, any future directed timelike curve in M_max from γ̃(s₀) to γ̃(s) is homotopic to γ̃|[s₀,s]'. The 'i.e.' needs every future timelike curve of M_max between two points of region I to stay in region I. That holds, since u and v increase along it (:800) and I = {u < 0, v > 0} (:673), but it is not said. In ETT the identification is stated on any open W (here ι(region I)), so it is not needed; this is the same remark as for Thm 4.9's reduction to Thm 4.10 (:809).

§1 and Thm 3.1 use opposite sign conventions for s₀. §1 writes the vertex γ̃(s₀) with s₀ < s < 0 (:146, :153). Thm 3.1 Step 1.2 takes s₀ ∈ (0, ε) with the vertex (−s₀, 0, …, 0) = γ̃(−s₀) (:528, :621). This is notational and harmless.

No defect in the causal skeleton itself. Steps (1)–(3) of Thm 3.1 (:485, :528, :619–621) and of Thm 4.10 (:1078) assemble with no hypothesis beyond those named here. The localisation used of M̃ is needed at the exit point γ̃(0) only (exitDiamonds_of_stronglyCausalOn), as Step 1.1 uses Lemma 2.4 only there. Thm 4.10's hypothesis (:785–788) need not include γ̃(0) ∉ ι(M_ext): the given-curve form does not use it, and it follows from v* → ∞ anyway.
questions: The ETT notion of an extension (Def 2.15). Reading taken: IsSpacetimeExtension CN C ι, i.e. an open embedding ι : N → M with range ι ≠ univ and ChartIso CN C along ι (so N's relations on every open U are those of ι(U) in M, Rem 2.3), with [Nonempty N]. Smoothness, the isometry and 'same dimension' enter only through these. Connectedness of N (Sbierski's tacit convention, :401) is not asked: only M preconnected is used, by Lemma 2.17. Whether the author wants more in the notion, for instance an IsEMorphism or a connectedness field, is left open.

The time-reversed alternative. Reading taken: the conclusion is for (D, DN) = (C, CN) or (C.dual, CN.dual). 'Future-inextensible' and the diamonds are read for D, so in the reversed case they are past-inextensibility and I⁻(γ s₀) ∩ I⁺(γ s) for C. This is Sbierski's 'otherwise reverse the time orientation' (:485, :798) taken literally.

The localisation at the exit point. Reading taken: the target's form uses LocallyStronglyCausal of M (the proposed node). exists_c0_extension_skeleton_of_frontier asks a strongly causal open neighbourhood of each frontier point only, and exitDiamonds_of_stronglyCausalOn asks it of γ 1 only. Which one the node and the binder's locally_strongly_causal should cite is the keeper's choice (T-lad-c0-extension-nodes).

The target text (and the binder's scheme) says 'W ⊊ M open' without non-emptiness. Reading taken: W is non-empty (hne). It is necessary, since for W = ∅ no curve starts in W, and it is implied by Sbierski's W = ι(M) for a manifold M (Def 2.15's footnote, :406). For the extension it is [Nonempty N].
kb_proposals: Sbierski 1507.00601's C⁰-extension skeleton (Thm 3.1, Thm 4.9, Thm 4.10, layer 1) is CausalScaffold.C0ExtensionSkeleton (T-abs-c0-extension-skeleton). Causality.ExitDiamonds W γ is the causal setting at the exit point: chart diamonds of compact closure and the identification, uniform over vertices r < s in [s₀, 1). exitDiamonds_of_curve is the given-curve form, exists_c0_extension_skeleton the leaving form. IsSpacetimeExtension (open embedding, proper range, ChartIso) is the ETT Def 2.15, and exists_c0_skeleton is its corollary.

To reparametrise a segment [r, s] of a curve over [0, 1]: CurveOn.restrict to [r, s], then CurveOn.comp_affine (k := s - r) (m := r) (a' := 0) (b' := 1), after rewriting (s - r) * 0 + r = r and (s - r) * 1 + r = s by ring. To get the tail γ([s₀, 1]) inside a neighbourhood: ContinuousWithinAt.preimage_mem_nhdsWithin, then mem_nhdsWithin_iff_exists_mem_nhds_inter and Metric.mem_nhds_iff, with s₀ = max 0 (1 - ε/2).

IsOpenEmbedding.toOpenPartialHomeomorph needs [Nonempty N]. Its simp lemma toOpenPartialHomeomorph_apply is a function equality (-fullyApplied): after rw [chartImage_top] at h, use simpa only [IsOpenEmbedding.toOpenPartialHomeomorph_apply] using h. Its source is univ (toOpenPartialHomeomorph_source), so every open set lies in chartSource.

ChartIso transports at the ETT layer: Causal.GXStructure has only the ≪ image (chronalCurveOn_image) and the inverse (curveOn_symm). The ≤ image is ChartIso.causalCurveOn_image (CausalScaffold.C0ExtensionSkeleton).
